“Pulaski Policy Papers” is a series of publications that focus on issues of great importance to Poland’s safety and stability, such as: global economy, Poland’s foreign policy and the political situation in Central and Eastern Europe.

The editor-in-chief of the Pulaski Policy Papers is Mr. Tomasz Smura (tsmura@pulaski.pl).

Published: August 26, 2026

What do Poland and the Republic of Korea (ROK) have in common? Despite the distance between the two and the fact that they are representative of and stand as the most successful nations economically, politically and militarily in their respective regions of the world, despite the two nations being the products of two entirely different cultures, the answer to that question of what they have in common is “a great deal.”

item.content:encoded:
The Russians are launching an attack along the border with Poland. Day 1665 of the war

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-24

Reports of Russian forces withdrawing to the Zherebets River line north of Lyman have been confirmed. This has eliminated the encirclement of Sloviansk from the north and has relatively levelled the front line. Most of the territory of the former breach has returned to Ukrainian control, though the Russians still maintain a broad bridgehead on the western bank of the river. According to some sources, the defenders also managed to carry out a series of successful counterattacks in the north-eastern part of Kharkiv Oblast, thereby averting the threat of their forces being encircled.

The Russians have captured part of the territory between the breaches made so far west of Pokrovsk, east of Dobropillia and west of Kostiantynivka, thereby limiting the potential threat posed by Ukrainian counterattacks. The flanking of Druzhkivka has intensified, whilst the invading forces have not achieved much success in Dobropillia or in Mykolaivka, which borders Sloviansk to the east. On 11 September, Russian guided aerial bombs destroyed the railway bridge connecting the eastern and western parts of Sloviansk (the road bridges had previously been destroyed).

Russian forces have entered the centre of Orikhiv, which is currently the scene of fighting. According to some sources, Mala Tokmachka, which neighbours Orikhiv to the east, has also come under their control. item.content:encoded:
Defence and International Security

发布源: 36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-24

The Pulaski Foundation Defence and Security Program provides multidisciplinary analysis of the current and emerging defense and security challenges facing the Transatlantic Alliance – with a special focus on Central and Eastern Europe.

Since 2022 the program allocates much of its resources to analysing the possible outcomes and consequences for European security of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. A special component of the program is devoted to the challenges and opportunities facing Poland’s defense policy, including modernizing of the Polish army and its industry. The main goal is to present actionable recommendations to an array of Polish stakeholders, including public administration, which could form a basis for long-term strategies for Poland in times of raising military and defense demands.

Overall, through its analysis, the program advocates for a stronger presence of NATO on the Alliance’s Eastern Flank, more developed European defence capabilities and argues for the need to provide military assistance and solid security guarantees to Ukraine.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Germany and the US expand defence industry cooperation

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-24

On 16 September, during a visit to the Pentagon, German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius (SPD) and his US counterpart, Pete Hegseth, signed a declaration on closer cooperation between the two countries’ defence industries and the harmonisation of military procurement regulations. They also discussed Germany’s plans to purchase the US Typhon ground-based long-range strike system, including Tomahawk cruise missiles with a range of 2,500 km. During his visit to the US, Pistorius also met representatives of US defence companies, senators and members of the House of Representatives. On 18 September, he attended the official handover of the first F-35A fighter aircraft to the German Air Force in Texas.

Germany seeks to reinforce its position as a key European ally of the US and demonstrate its readiness to assume greater responsibility for defence and deterrence within NATO. Berlin also aims to deepen defence industrial cooperation with Washington. It views the presence of US defence companies in Germany as a potential means of ensuring continued US engagement in the security of NATO’s European members. Closer cooperation is also expected to strengthen Berlin’s position within the Alliance and enhance the competitiveness of German companies working with US partners.

item.title: [19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland] Russia’s war plan: subjugate Ukraine, intimidate Europe, buy off the US
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Russia’s war plan: subjugate Ukraine, intimidate Europe, buy off the US

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-24

Russia is preparing to escalate its aggression against Ukraine and launch a new phase of its so-called hybrid war against Europe. The Kremlin is pursuing this course because it remains unable to achieve its objectives and faces mounting domestic challenges. At the same time, it remains confident of victory, basing this assessment on the perceived weaknesses of its adversaries – Ukraine and the West.

Russia’s first objective is to continue devastating Ukraine and force its de facto capitulation so as to subjugate the country. Second, Moscow is striving to weaken and intimidate European countries in order to curb their support for Ukraine, undermine sanctions pressure on Russia and foment domestic instability. This would create conditions for dismantling the existing European security order and expanding Russian penetration of the continent. Third, it aims to manipulate and ‘buy off’ the Trump administration by offering the prospect of lucrative business deals, seeking to induce Washington to end all support for Ukraine, lift sanctions against Russia and resume cooperation with Moscow, thereby strengthening Vladimir Putin’s regime.

For these reasons, further Russian escalation is inevitable, although Western countries could seek to limit its scale by strengthening both their resilience and their capacity to deter Moscow, including by significantly raising the costs of its aggressive policies through retaliatory measures.
